prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

Summary of 2001 manifesto proposals (ideological framing and names omitted)

- Family and education
  - Targeted tax cuts: higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; transferable allowance for couples with young children or caring responsibilities; remove tax on Widowed Parent benefits; reform in‑work credit to be paid to the caring parent.
  - School autonomy (“Free Schools”): heads/governors control staffing, pay, admissions via home–school agreements; easier exclusion for disruptive pupils with off-site Progress Centres; successful schools free to expand; new schools allowed from faith, parent, charitable and company providers; parents can trigger special inspections and management change; redirect bureaucracy savings directly to schools.
  - Students and universities: raise loan repayment threshold to £20,000; no top‑up fees; create university endowments.

- Crime and justice
  - Increase police numbers; cut bureaucracy; visible policing (e.g., paperwork done on the beat); parish constables; focus on antisocial behaviour.
  - Expand secure training places for persistent young offenders; link release to behaviour/qualifications.
  - Mandatory prison for selling drugs to under‑16s; tougher sentences near schools.
  - End automatic early release; require prison work with proceeds to victims/families.
  - Lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; protect children online.
  - Stronger victim rights: named contacts in police/CPS; written reasons if charges dropped; update self‑defence and double jeopardy rules.

- Economy and regulation
  - Tax reductions funded by £8bn in savings (excluding schools/NHS/police/defence): abolish taxes on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; married couple’s allowance; higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; cut fuel duty by at least 6p/litre; business rates cuts; abolish IR35; targeted regeneration breaks; relief for approved share options.
  - Simpler, more transparent tax/accounts; Capital Gains Tax simplification with lower rates.
  - Deregulation Commission with departmental regulatory budgets; small-firm exemptions; focus utility regulators on competition.
  - Replace Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear’s role.
  - Keep the pound; bolster monetary policy independence; external fiscal scrutiny.

- Health
  - Match planned NHS funding but shift control to clinicians; Patient’s Guarantee of maximum waits based on clinical need with right to alternative NHS/private provision; more choice for patients/GPs; empower ward sisters/matrons; expand practice nurse roles; specialist surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund; increase hospice funding; remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable.

- Older people and care
  - Raise basic state pension (larger uplift for over‑75s); option to consolidate certain payments into a higher tax‑free pension; increase age allowance by £2,000 to remove ~1m from income tax; abolish compulsory annuitisation at 75; explore funded pension option for younger workers; protect assets for those who pre‑fund long‑term care.

- International and defence
  - In the EU but retain veto; keep the pound; seek treaty flexibility/reserved powers; strengthen the single market and anti‑fraud measures.
  - Prioritise NATO; oppose separate EU military structures; maintain independent deterrent; support missile defence; reach full manning; reserves reform; exempt armed forces from certain human rights constraints as other states do.
  - Aid: work toward 0.7% GNP; double share via charities; improve EU aid or permit bilateral alternatives; push debt relief, HIV/AIDS, conflict resolution; envoy for religious freedom.
  - Trade: pursue EU‑NAFTA free trade area toward global free trade by 2020; align diplomacy and trade promotion.

- Asylum
  - House new applicants in secure reception centres pending decisions; presume refusal for safe‑country claims; create a removals agency for rejected cases.

- Welfare and civil society
  - Office of Civil Society; eliminate irrecoverable VAT for charities.
  - Replace existing job schemes with outcome‑based contracts paying for sustained employment; “can work, must work” principle; lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work.
  - Improve disabled savings rules; new Incapacity Benefit agency funding rehabilitation; national anti‑fraud squad; clean up National Insurance numbers.

- Town, country, transport, environment
  - Foot‑and‑mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP with more national/local control; honest food labelling; reduce rural red tape; cut business rates for key rural services; benefit card to sustain post offices; support rural transport.
  - Abolish top‑down housebuilding targets; more local control; protect green/“blue belt” areas; rural affairs select committee.
  - Urban regeneration companies with powers over policing, schools, planning, and housing renewal; promote brownfield building; expand homeownership (right‑to‑buy, rent‑to‑mortgage, homesteading).
  - Transport: long‑term plans; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe with strict enforcement; charge foreign lorries; revive rail; cut fuel duty; promote cleaner fuels/vehicles.
  - Environment: emissions trading, conservation, renewables, cleaner generation.

- Culture, media, sport
  - Privatise Channel 4; £3bn endowment for cultural bodies; simplify lottery rules; strengthen tourism promotion.
  - Protect school sport time/playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; streamline funding.
  - Single media/communications regulator; modernise ownership rules; independent BBC regulation; fair access for religious broadcasters.

- Democracy and governance
  - Devolve powers to high‑performing “free councils”; fewer central targets; local referendums on large council tax rises.
  - Abolish regional agencies/assemblies; return development powers locally.
  - English votes for English laws; strengthen Lords with independent appointments and elected element; enhance Commons scrutiny (more frequent PM accountability, stronger select committees); retain current general election voting system.
  - Reduce numbers of ministers, MPs (after scrutiny reforms), and political advisers.

TEXT_G:
Summary of policy proposals (2001)

- Constitutional and governance
  - Seek a referendum on full self-government and expanded powers for the Scottish Parliament.
  - Create a written constitution; inclusive citizenship based on residence, birth, or parentage; retain the monarchy subject to referendum.
  - Introduce proportional representation at all levels; reform and reduce quangos; strengthen parliamentary oversight.
  - Ensure civil service career continuity and advancement in Scotland.

- Economy, investment, and taxation
  - Establish a sovereign wealth-style fund using surplus oil revenues (Scottish Fund for Future Generations).
  - Create a public, not-for-profit infrastructure financier (Scottish Trust for Public Investment) to replace high-cost PFI/PPP.
  - Conduct a comprehensive tax review focused on fairness, simplicity, and business competitiveness; no overall tax rise without mandate.
  - Immediate measures: cut fuel duty by 10p/gal, funded by a new 5p income tax band on earnings over £100,000; consider small business rates relief; review local government finance, including local income tax.

- Jobs, wages, and enterprise
  - Raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages, with support for small firms via tax measures; strengthen trade union rights through a statutory charter.
  - Devolve and refocus employment programs toward training and job black spots.
  - Invest in transport, digital connectivity, and skills; streamline development agencies; integrate tourism promotion into the enterprise network.

- Education and children
  - Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants; support Cubie recommendations on student benefits.
  - Create an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18 in stages; end league tables; cut assessment burdens; major school refurbishment via the public investment trust.
  - Lower voting age to 16; implement UNCRC; establish a Children’s Commissioner; expand Gaelic-medium education; support inclusive education and anti-racism.

- Health and social care
  - Form a National Health Care Commission to set strategy and end postcode treatment by making HTBS decisions binding; increase HTBS budget.
  - Public health: free fruit in primary schools; nutritional standards for school meals.
  - Reintroduce free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges.
  - Invest via the public investment trust; audit and modernize equipment; £4m Clean Hospitals Fund; recruit at least 1,500 nurses; halve maximum inpatient waits; provide free personal care for older people.

- Environment, energy, and water
  - Climate risk assessment and a National Environment Plan; target 12% of total energy (25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010.
  - No new nuclear plants; decommission existing sites; develop decommissioning expertise.
  - Promote waste reduction and polluter-pays principles; review climate levy impacts on hydro.
  - Review water industry finances to curb charge increases; enhance democratic control; protect low-income users; seek Competition Act exemption.

- Justice, drugs, and policing
  - Fund 1,000 additional police officers; establish a Sentencing Advisory Panel; speed up lower courts.
  - Expand drug courts; strengthen rehabilitation and family support.
  - Parental compensation orders for youth damage (with safeguards).
  - Lifetime supervision for high-risk violent/sexual offenders; implement Maclean recommendations; strengthen sex offender registration.

- Social policy, equality, and immigration
  - National anti-poverty strategy with “poverty-proofing”; shift social inclusion admin funds to frontline services.
  - Fast and fair asylum decisions; oppose voucher-based support.
  - Strengthen disability rights (extend DDA scope; introduce a disability equality indicator).

- Housing and communities
  - Press for UK assumption of historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via the public investment trust.
  - Oppose wholesale stock transfer; support tenant-focused, tenure-neutral policy; three-year core funding for voluntary sector; exempt charities from water charges.
  - Tackle rough sleeping and hidden homelessness.

- Rural, agriculture, fisheries, and land
  - Immediate 10p/gal fuel duty cut; improve rural transport and digital access; protect post offices, schools, and links.
  - Post–foot and mouth agricultural review; tighten import controls and origin labelling; support diversification and organics; renegotiate Less Favoured Areas terms.
  - Fisheries: compensated tie-ups; technical conservation; devolved leadership in EU talks; reform CFP toward zonal management; support processing and aquaculture.
  - Independent inquiry on salmon farming; strengthen environmental regulation; enhance SEPA resources.
  - Expand community land rights and participation; develop a national freshwater fisheries policy.

- Europe, defence, and international
  - Support EU membership with stronger subsidiarity; consider euro entry subject to conditions and referendum.
  - Remove nuclear weapons from Scotland; oppose US missile defence; create a professional Scottish Defence Force; phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining cooperation.
  - Refocus external representation on trade, investment, and tourism; raise aid toward UN targets; cancel debt; untie aid; coordinate NGOs via “Aid from Scotland.”

- Transport and connectivity
  - Use the public investment trust for rail electrification (including East Coast), airport rail links, Borders rail, and key bottlenecks; create Regional Transport Authorities; single multimodal safety body; keep air traffic control public; public stake in Railtrack for accountability.
  - National concessionary travel for youth, students, older and disabled people; explore light rail.
  - Reduce ferry fares via Road Equivalent Tariff pilots; abolish Skye Bridge tolls; airports review to increase direct European flights and reduce fares.

- Culture, language, broadcasting, and sport
  - Devolve broadcasting oversight; accelerate digital rollout; increase autonomy for national public broadcaster.
  - Reform arts funding; establish a national theatre and a “Scottish Academy”; boost traditional arts; create a national lottery.
  - Support Gaelic and Scots languages in education and media.
  - Prioritize community sport; support football academies; bid to host major tournaments.

- Pensions and social security
  - Restore the earnings link for the basic state pension, using NI Fund surplus; protect those near tax thresholds; aim to align basic pension with MIG over time.
  - Streamline benefits delivery into a single agency; simplify housing benefit and use it to lower housing costs; improve disability benefit processing; consider extending winter fuel payments to severely disabled under 60; review support for 16–17 year olds; improve Working Families Tax Credit design and uptake.
